item.title: HTML5 diagrams.show:right — vertical stacking layout with direction config option
item.justification:
When html5.diagrams.show is set to "right", chord diagram boxes are placed horizontally adjacent to the song content. This crowds the layout when more than one or two chords are used, as the boxes spill into the song area. A vertical column (boxes stacked below each other) is the natural expectation for a right-side chord panel.
Root cause: .cp-chord-diagrams uses display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap (horizontal row-wrap). When show:right, the diagrams panel is an auto-width grid column so diagrams never wrap and spread horizontally without constraint.
Additionally, a config key (html5.diagrams.direction: vertical|horizontal) should allow users to explicitly choose the arrangement, so that horizontal layout remains accessible for compact songbooks that prefer it.

capabilities.capability: Default vertical stacking for chord diagrams when diagrams.show:right is configured.
New html5.diagrams.direction config key (vertical|horizontal) for user override.

technical-parameters.constraint: CSS change must apply to both standard and paged HTML5 output (paged CSS includes html5/css/chord-diagrams.tt directly via content.tt — see L-5).
Config key lives under html5.diagrams (not pdf.diagrams); lookup follows existing html5_diagrams->{key} pattern in HTML5.pm.

Default direction is "vertical" when show:right; when direction is not set, CSS rule .cp-song-layout-right .cp-chord-diagrams { flex-direction: column } provides the default without requiring a class.
technical-parameters.nfr: Direction class naming follows the existing cp-chord-diagrams-align-{value} pattern already in the codebase.
technical-parameters.pattern: Add CSS class cp-chord-diagrams-direction-vertical / cp-chord-diagrams-direction-horizontal alongside the existing align classes (L-5: fix consistently in chord-diagrams.tt so both standard and paged templates inherit the rule).

Pass diagrams_direction from render_chord_diagrams() to the chord_diagrams template, parallel to existing diagrams_align parameter (L-7: preview mode inherits same CSS so screen and print stay aligned).

tasks.task: In lib/ChordPro/res/templates/html5/chord-diagrams.tt, add the direction class to the cp-chord-diagrams div: [% IF diagrams_direction %] cp-chord-diagrams-direction-[% diagrams_direction | html %][% END %] (Added alongside existing cp-chord-diagrams-align-{value} class.)
Run `make` to regenerate lib/ChordPro/Config/Data.pm from the updated chordpro.json. Verify the new html5.diagrams.direction key appears in the generated Data.pm.

Extend t/86_html5_diagram_pos.t with two new sub-tests: (a) show:right with default config → CSS contains .cp-song-layout-right .cp-chord-diagrams and flex-direction:column rule; no explicit direction class required. (b) show:right with html5.diagrams.direction:"horizontal" → output contains class cp-chord-diagrams-direction-horizontal. Follow the existing run_position_test() helper pattern. Update plan tests => N count.

entry.note: Root cause confirmed: flex-wrap:wrap horizontal default in .cp-chord-diagrams. Fix via CSS default rule + direction class + html5.diagrams.direction config key. Lessons L-5, L-7 applied.

r.observations: chordpro.json has two html5 { } blocks that are merged last-wins; the diagrams key had to be added to the SECOND block (the one with mode:"print") because the second block overwrites the first entirely. cfgboot.pl must be run directly (perl script/cfgboot.pl) to regenerate Data.pm since `make resources` skips it when Data.pm is newer than chordpro.json. The built-in default config sets html5.diagrams.direction:"vertical", so the direction class IS emitted for the default case (not absent as initially expected in the test).
r.lessons-learned: When chordpro.json has duplicate top-level keys (both html5 { } blocks), JSON::Relaxed uses last-wins and the entire value is replaced — not merged. Any new key must go in the LAST occurrence of the duplicate. Run `perl script/cfgboot.pl <json> -o <Data.pm>` directly rather than `make resources` to force-regenerate Data.pm.

item.title: HTML5 grid strum lines are not rendered as arrow rows
item.steps-to-reproduce: 1. Create a song with a strum grid line as documented in docs/content/Directives-env_grid.md (`|s dn~up ...`). 2. Run: perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl --generate=HTML5 testing/strum-repro.cho --output=testing/strum-repro.html 3. Inspect generated HTML body. 4. Observe only regular chord grid lines are rendered; the strum line is missing (or appears as plain pseudo-chord text in affected paths), and no up/down arrow symbols are shown.
item.expected-result: For `start_of_grid` strum rows, HTML5 output should render a visible strum row with strum symbols (up/down arrows and variants) per directive docs, not omit the row and not degrade to raw pseudo-chord codes.
item.analysis:
Code-based root cause: - Parser path (`lib/ChordPro/Song.pm`, `decompose_grid`) marks strum rows as `type => "strumline"` (with optional `subtype => "cellbars"` for uppercase `S`) while converting pseudo-chords to `ChordPro::Chord::Strum` chord objects. - HTML5 renderer (`lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm`, `_process_song_body`) handles `type eq 'gridline'` but has no handler for `type eq 'strumline'`. - As a result, strum rows are not rendered in HTML5 grid output, so expected strum glyphs never appear.
Evidence: - Reproduction with `testing/strum-repro.cho` produces a `<div class="cp-grid">` with only the regular chord line in `testing/strum-repro.html`; the strum line is absent. - PDF grid renderer (`lib/ChordPro/Output/PDF/Grid.pm`) explicitly uses line type/subtype and grid-strum font handling, confirming intended behavior exists in another backend.

tasks.task: Add HTML5 handling for `type => strumline` in `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm` so strum grid rows are rendered instead of skipped.
Implement strumline rendering semantics for lowercase/uppercase marker behavior (`|s` vs `|S`) using existing token metadata (`subtype => cellbars`) so bar/cell visibility aligns with directive docs.
Ensure strum tokens render using strum display glyphs (`ChordPro::Chord::Strum->chord_display`) rather than raw pseudo-chord codes in HTML5 output.
Adjust/add HTML5 CSS classes only as needed to preserve legibility of strum rows without regressing normal grid rendering.
Add regression tests for HTML5 strum grids (including `|s` and `|S` cases) and verify mirrored bugfix suites stay aligned where applicable.

test.description: HTML5 grid with strum rows renders visible strum output.
test.assertions: Generated HTML contains a rendered strum grid row and includes strum glyph output rather than raw `dn`/`up` pseudo-chord text.

test.description: Mirrored HTML5 bugfix suite stays consistent for strum-row behavior.
test.assertions: Equivalent strum-row rendering assertions pass in mirrored suite.

test.description: Render a documented strum example from Directives-env_grid and visually compare expected arrow-style output.
test.assertions: Strum row is present and arrows are shown; no silent row drop in HTML5 output.

entry.note: Assigned to DEV for HTML5 strumline rendering fix and regressions. Branch: bug/item-44-html5-grid-strumline-arrow-rendering
Added HTML5 strumline dispatch/rendering path, strum-specific classes, lowercase/uppercase bar visibility handling, and mirrored regressions; focused suites PASS.

Lowercase `|s` strum rows render without bar symbols, while uppercase `|S` (`subtype=cellbars`) keeps bars visible, aligning with documented semantics. Regression tests confirm strum row presence/class and no breakage in existing delegate/diagram behavior.

item.title: HTML5 paired chord/strum grid lines drift out of cell alignment vs PDF
item.steps-to-reproduce: 1. Create a grid that alternates chord rows and strum rows, e.g.: {start_of_grid shape="0+2x4+0"} | C ~Am . . | F . . . | |s dn~up dn~up ~up dn~up | dn~up dn~up ~up dn~up | | G/B . . . | C . . . | |S d+~u+ ~up d+~u+ ~up | d+~u+ ~up d+~u+ ~ux | {end_of_grid} 2. Generate both outputs: perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl --generate=PDF testing/strum-sync-repro.cho --output=testing/strum-sync-repro.pdf perl -Ilib script/chordpro.pl --generate=HTML5 testing/strum-sync-repro.cho --output=testing/strum-sync-repro.html 3. Compare the same measures in PDF and HTML5 output. 4. Observe in HTML5 that strum symbols/chords can shift horizontally relative to the chord row cell boundaries (especially with mixed token widths), while PDF keeps both rows cell-aligned.
item.expected-result: In HTML5, strum rows and chord rows within a grid should remain measure/cell synchronized like PDF output: each strum symbol aligns with the corresponding chord cell, with `|s`/`|S` bar visibility semantics preserved.
item.analysis:
Code-based root cause: - Item 44 fixed missing strumline rendering, but HTML5 still lays out each row as independent inline/flex content (`render_gridline` + `.cp-gridline`), not a shared cell geometry. - Current HTML5 CSS (`tab-grid.tt`) uses `display:flex` with token gap and content-driven widths (`.cp-grid-chord { min-width: 3em; }`), so token widths vary by text length and symbol class. - PDF grid rendering (`lib/ChordPro/Output/PDF/Grid.pm::gridline`) advances by fixed `cellwidth`/`barwidth`, ensuring deterministic x positions across paired chord/strum rows. - Because HTML5 lacks an explicit per-cell column model shared between adjacent `gridline` and `strumline`, rows with the same musical structure can visually desynchronize.
Evidence: - `render_gridline` emits a linear `<span class="cp-grid-tokens">` stream without explicit cell index wrappers or shape-based columns. - Paired rows with mixed-width tokens (e.g., `G/B`, repeats, multi-strum tokens) produce visibly different token spacing in HTML5 compared to PDF.
Security/privacy and vulnerability check: - AUTH/NETWORK/CRYPTO: not applicable for this rendering bug. - INPUT/DATA/DISCLOSURE: preserve existing `escape_text` behavior and avoid introducing raw HTML injection while restructuring grid markup.
Collision check: - No current APPROVED or IN_PROGRESS items exist in `overview-features-bugs.xml`; planned file overlap risk is currently none.

Refactor HTML5 gridline/strumline markup emission in `lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5.pm` to carry explicit per-cell structure (or equivalent deterministic column indexing) rather than pure content-width flow.
Update HTML5 grid CSS (`tab-grid.tt`) so paired grid rows share a stable column model and render aligned cell positions for both chord and strum rows.
Preserve existing `|s` vs `|S` behavior (bar/cell-line visibility) and existing glyph conversion for strum pseudo-chords while introducing alignment changes.
Add/extend regressions in mirrored HTML5 bugfix suites to assert paired-line structural alignment invariants, not just strum-row presence.
Perform manual PDF-vs-HTML5 visual comparison on a representative mixed-token strum grid to validate practical parity.

item.title: HTML5 diagrams show:right breaks right-panel box sizing and alignment
item.steps-to-reproduce: 1. Configure diagrams on the right (e.g. `pdf.diagrams.show: right`, optionally `html5.diagrams.direction: vertical`). 2. Generate HTML5 output for a song with multiple chord diagrams and regular body content. 3. Open the generated HTML and inspect the song layout and chord-diagram panel. 4. Observe the right diagrams panel/box appears misaligned and/or visually smaller than contained chord images in affected songs; overall right-side layout can look broken.
item.expected-result: When diagrams are shown on the right, the right panel should stay consistently right-aligned and its surrounding box should fully contain diagram images without overflow/collapse artifacts.
item.analysis: Code-based hypothesis with evidence: - Existing right-side mode is implemented by applying `cp-song-layout-right` to the whole song container (`song.tt`), with CSS grid declared in `css/chord-diagrams.tt`: `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto`. - Because the grid is on `.cp-song` (which also contains title/metadata/body/other blocks), right-layout sizing/alignment behavior is sensitive to all direct child content, not only the intended body+diagram pair. - Current right-panel rules (`.cp-song-layout-right .cp-song-diagrams { align-self: start; }`) do not explicitly enforce horizontal alignment strategy (`justify-self`) or panel width constraints for containment behavior. - Diagram rendering now uses `` (item 43), while panel styling was originally tuned around prior behavior; right-panel containment/alignment regressions can surface when the panel is auto-sized next to wide content. Observed evidence from local reproduction: - Generated HTML shows `cp-song cp-song-layout-right` with `cp-song-body` and `cp-song-diagrams`, but visual right-panel alignment/box containment remains inconsistent in user-reported cases. - Existing regression `t/86_html5_diagram_pos.t` validates presence of right-layout classes and direction behavior, but does not assert panel-width containment or right-edge alignment invariants. Security/privacy and vulnerability assessment: - AUTH/NETWORK/CRYPTO: not applicable for this CSS/layout bug. - INPUT/DATA/DISCLOSURE: preserve current escaping and avoid introducing raw HTML/CSS injection paths while modifying templates/styles. Collision analysis: - `overview-features-bugs.xml` currently has no APPROVED or IN_PROGRESS item-refs; no hard resource conflicts detected for planned modified source files.

tasks.task: Reproduce the right-panel issue with a deterministic fixture and capture structural + visual evidence (container width, alignment, and image containment).
Refine right-layout structure/rules so only intended song-body+diagram sections participate in the two-column layout semantics (without disturbing title/metadata flow).
Update right-panel CSS in `css/chord-diagrams.tt` to enforce robust right alignment and containment (panel sizing constraints and child overflow behavior).
Verify `cp-diagram-svg` sizing behavior remains consistent for image-based diagrams and does not regress bottom/top diagram placements.
Extend `t/86_html5_diagram_pos.t` with assertions for right-panel containment/alignment invariants in addition to existing class checks.
Add mirrored regression coverage in `t/html5/09_bugfixes.t` and `t/190_html5_bugfixes.t` only if layout invariant cannot be fully captured in `t/86_html5_diagram_pos.t` alone.

test.assertions: HTML/CSS output proves right-panel uses stable alignment and containment rules (no panel/image mismatch) while preserving direction classes and existing placement behavior.

item.title: Retire deprecated ABC handler alias usage in test paths and stabilize warning-free runs
item.justification:
The full-test run repeatedly emits: ABC: Please remove handler "ChordPro::Delegate::ABC" from your ABC delegates config and use "abc2svg" instead. Although tests still pass, this warning noise indicates legacy handler values are still reachable in test execution paths. Leaving this unresolved has ongoing costs: - Warning spam obscures real failures in CI/local logs. - Test outcomes depend on ambient config state (e.g., user/system config), reducing reproducibility. - Delegate handler migration remains incomplete, increasing maintenance burden for future ABC changes.
This debt item aligns runtime/test behavior with the current delegate contract (`abc2svg` / quickjs variants) and makes warning-free test output deterministic.

technical-parameters.constraint: Preserve backward compatibility for real user configs while eliminating warning churn in repository test runs.
Do not change delegate rendering behavior for valid handlers (`abc2svg`, `quickjs`, `quickjs_xs`, `quickjs_qjs`).
Keep tests environment-independent: avoid reliance on host user/system config for expected output (L-15, L-16).
technical-parameters.nfr: Reduce log noise so warnings become actionable signals rather than expected background output.
Ensure repeated `make test`/`make tests` runs are deterministic across developer machines and CI.
technical-parameters.pattern: Apply backend-aware delegate conventions introduced in item 37 and avoid reintroducing module-name handlers (L-11).

item.analysis:
Observed evidence: - Full-test log shows repeated warning lines near `t/80_pages.t`..`t/88_pages.t`, each warning referencing deprecated handler `ChordPro::Delegate::ABC`. - Warning is emitted by `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/ABC.pm::info()` when the resolved handler is not in the accepted set and is normalized to `abc2svg`.
Likely debt surface: - Some test execution path still resolves an old handler value (module-name style), directly or via merged external config. - Page tests currently use `--no-default-configs` but may still be sensitive to user/system config state unless explicitly disabled.
Scope of remediation: 1) Identify the exact source(s) of deprecated handler value in test runs. 2) Normalize test invocation/config so repository tests do not inherit legacy handler values from ambient environment. 3) Keep compatibility behavior for external users while ensuring project tests are warning-clean by default.

tasks.task: Trace warning provenance end-to-end in test runs (which test invocation path resolves handler `ChordPro::Delegate::ABC`, and whether source is repository config, generated config, or host/user config merge).

Harden affected tests (notably page-sequence tests around t/80_pages.t..t/88_pages.t) to run with explicit config isolation (`--no-userconfig` and `--no-sysconfig` where appropriate) so host state cannot reintroduce deprecated handler warnings.

If warning source is internal fallback logic, update `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/ABC.pm` (and related delegate resolution code if needed) to canonicalize legacy handler aliases earlier while preserving compatibility and avoiding repeated warning emissions during a single run.
Add/extend regression coverage to assert warning-free behavior for the affected test path and to confirm ABC delegate output still works with supported handlers.
Update delegate configuration documentation/examples if any project-owned sample still advertises deprecated handler/module-name patterns.

test.description: Representative page-test path executes without deprecated ABC handler warning under controlled config.
test.assertions: Test passes and output stream does not contain `Please remove handler "ChordPro::Delegate::ABC"`.

test.description: HTML5 delegate path remains functional with supported ABC handler resolution.
test.assertions: Delegate rendering assertions pass and no deprecated-handler warning appears from repository-controlled config.

test.description: Re-run `make tests` and verify warning count for deprecated ABC handler is zero in the generated log.
test.assertions: Suite result remains PASS/expected skips and deprecated ABC warning string is absent.

security-assessment.category: No authentication boundary changes; risk unchanged.
Ensure handler canonicalization does not broaden accepted untrusted values beyond documented handlers.
No persistent data model changes expected.
No privilege boundary changes; test isolation should reduce accidental host-config coupling.
Reducing warning noise lowers risk of missing important diagnostics, but no direct data disclosure changes.

impact-check.shared-feature: External delegate integration is directly affected; handler canonicalization and config isolation must keep existing delegate behavior stable.
HTML5 delegate tests are part of the warning surface, so regressions must be checked in HTML5-specific suites.
